content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts tend to overestimate prices in bullish event periods, especially when sentiment is high.", "Forecast bias is amplified when supply net is negative and bullish events outnumber bearish ones.", "Sentiment spikes often precede price corrections, indicating model overreaction to short-term sentiment.", "Mean-reversion is stronger in high-event periods with negative supply net, causing forecasts to lag true price movements.", "Forecast accuracy declines when sentiment is inconsistent or mixed, especially near auction periods.", "Model forecasts should adjust downward when bearish sentiment dominates despite bullish event counts.", "Price overshoots are common in early forecast windows when event balance is negative and sentiment is volatile.", "Forecast calibration should incorporate recent price volatility and sentiment alignment with event-driven supply changes."]}
